findings.title: Passkeys are enabled only when a user is already set, which is the reverse of the intended condition
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` ends with `&& user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn form when `context.getUser() == null`, which is a normal first login. Both new call sites now pass `context.getUser()`. On a fresh login the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is never called and the conditional-UI passkey form is missing. The same happens in `challenge(...)` after a bad password when the user was cleared. Only the re-authentication case, where the user is already set, gets passkeys. The tests in this PR expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial login page, so they would fail. Allow a null user: `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. If re-authentication needs extra conditions, apply them only when the user is non-null.
